To perform a dental implant, a surgical procedure must be carried out in the jaw where the implant should be placed.  Once the process is completed, a type of screw called an abutment will be placed on top of the implant.  This is then joined by the prosthesis, which is attached to it via either the abutment or through a crown, a tooth-shaped piece of dental hardware that can either be cemented to the head of the implant or attached to the root-end of the implant.  Once this is completed, the implant is considered fully fixed and can now support a dental prosthesis.
